memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But God came to Abimelek in a dream one night and said to him, "You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken; she is a married woman." Now Abimelek had not gone near her, so he said, "Lord, will you destroy an innocent nation?" - Gen 20:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Something surprising happens here. God comes and speaks - not to Abraham, His chosen servant, but to Abimelech, a pagan king. In a dream, God warns this outsider of the danger he is in, protecting him from unknowingly committing a grave sin. God is at work in the life of a man who is not part of the covenant, watching over him with care.

This tells us something wonderful about God's reach. His concern is not confined to His own people. He speaks to Abimelech, restrains him, and even shields him from wrongdoing he did not intend. God is sovereign over the hearts and lives of all people, believers and unbelievers alike.

Notice too Abimelech's response: "Lord, will you destroy an innocent nation?" This pagan king appeals to God's justice - and, remarkably, in this instance his conscience is clearer than Abraham's conduct. God's people do not have a monopoly on decency, and sometimes the outsider behaves better than the insider.

This should humble us and enlarge our vision of God. He is at work far beyond the walls of the church, speaking to consciences, restraining evil, drawing people we might overlook. "The Lord is good to all; he has compassion on all he has made" (Ps 145:9). Never assume God is absent from the life of an unbeliever. He may be working in ways we cannot see, preparing hearts we've written off.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you limit God's work to His own people, or see Him at work beyond?
- Has an "outsider" ever put your own conduct to shame?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that Your reach extends far beyond Your own people. You speak to consciences and restrain evil everywhere. Enlarge my vision to see You at work in the lives of those I might overlook.
Amen.
